name: Moss
description: Water retention intelligence through fractal surface area maximization. Achieves desiccation tolerance via anhydrobiosis — entering suspended animation when dry and reviving when wet, surviving for decades in cryptobiotic state. Colonizes bare rock through rhizoid anchoring without true roots, capturing atmospheric nutrients directly. Engineers moisture-gradient microhabitats that enable succession of larger plant communities.

core_attributes.pattern: capillary water retention, cryptobiotic desiccation tolerance, atmospheric nutrient capture

scope.definition: Desiccation tolerance and revival efficiency of Sphagnum moss — fraction of metabolic function recovered within 12 hours of rehydration after complete air-drying (>95% water loss).

evidence.source: Proctor (2008) 'Physiological ecology: water relations, light and temperature responses, carbon balance', in 'Bryophyte Biology', 2nd ed., Cambridge UP; Bewley (1979) 'Physiological aspects of desiccation tolerance' Annual Review Plant Physiology.
cross_domain_examples: Sphagnum revival from complete desiccation: 0.84-0.92 of maximal photosynthesis restored within 6-12h
Tortula ruralis: 0.97 of net photosynthesis restored within 1 hour of rehydration after years dry
tardigrade cryptobiosis: analogous complete metabolic suspension and high-fidelity revival

scope.falsifiability: If rehydrated mosses show <40% of original photosynthetic rates after 24h in controlled conditions, desiccation tolerance does not extend to photosynthetic machinery.
scope.measurement_limits: Revival efficiency varies widely by moss species — Sphagnum (bog moss) is more sensitive than Tortula (desert moss). Multi-day desiccation recovery is slightly lower than single-day desiccation recovery.
